messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=infra.gpu-hosts (sev=P1) — reason: kernel panic on host gpu-node-fs-03, kubelet NotReady, node unreachable. PD: https://pagerduty.example/c/incidents/PD12345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Reminder: runbook -> https://redwood-internal/runbooks/gpu-node-kernel-panic. Escalation policy: oncall -> oncall+1 in 15m if no ack.

alex: acked. I'm on it.

alex: quick summary of what I see: host stopped heartbeating at 02:07 UTC. Node in k8s shows "NotReady" and last kernel message shows OOPS/panic. SSH attempts time out. Pod restarts on serving-prod increased ~12% in the last 5m. API 502s up from 0.3% -> 6%.

maria: verified customer-facing metrics: embeddings and completion endpoints show elevated error rates. Ops dashboard flagged 3 Dedicated customers with >10% request errors in last 10m. I'm notifying support.

samir: do we have any automated fallback? routing policy for low-latency tier should fallback to secondary rack, but looks like some traffic pinned to this node's pod replicas.

alex: kubelet dead so "kubectl drain" will fail. Options: 1) scale up deployments in affected namespaces to get new pods scheduled on healthy nodes, 2) force-delete pods that are stuck on the dead node so controllers recreate them elsewhere. I'll try #1 first to avoid aggressive deletes.

alex: running: 
```
kubectl -n serving-prod scale deploy model-serving --replicas=20
# increasing replicas to push new pods onto healthy nodes
```

maria: good. I'll open a customer incident for the three affected accounts and link status page.

jin: I can patch ingress/routing to steer traffic away from the affected replica-set if needed. Might be simpler to do short-term routing change while pods stabilize.

samir: if scaling doesn't catch up, we should force-delete stuck pods. Command: 
```
kubectl delete pod <pod-name> -n serving-prod --grace-period=0 --force
```
Use cautiously — will trigger immediate restarts.

alex: scaling helped — new pods are Pending -> Running on other hosts. Error rate dropping to ~2.1% now. Still seeing few 502s where requests hit the node-local cache.

incident-bot: host reboot request queued with infra-ops. Ticket INFRA-4972 created (reprovision + hardware diag).

samir: infra-ops action: power cycle scheduled in 12 minutes, then NIC diagnostics.

maria: customer comms: status page updated -> "We are experiencing elevated errors for inference endpoints; mitigation in progress. Working with SRE. No data loss expected."

ops-bot: Auto-escalation suppressed: incident acknowledged and active.

alex: one more note: several pods on the dead node used local GPU-attached storage for cache. Those caches will be lost; we should warm caches on the replacement pods. I'll trigger cache-warm job.

alex: running cache warm job: 
```
kubectl -n serving-prod rollout restart job/cold-cache-warmup
```

jin: infra-ops confirms power-cycle started. Also kicking off host reprovision if reboot fails.

maria: Support: opened tickets and pinged account owners for the three Dedicated customers. CC: enterprise-ops.

samir: any ETA on full recovery? If reboot works, we should see node rejoin in ~10-15m; if not, reprovision could be 45-90m.

alex: agreed. Current mitigation: traffic rebalanced, error rate back to ~0.5-1.5%. Still monitoring.

alex: handing off primary response to jin (next oncall) — summarized actions: 
- Node gpu-node-fs-03 kernel panic, ssh unreachable, kubelet NotReady. PD incident PD12345.
- Infra ticket INFRA-4972: power-cycle in progress, reprovision path ready.
- Mitigation taken: scaled model-serving -> 20 replicas; forced replacement pods starting on healthy nodes; cache-warm job triggered.
- Customer impact: 3 Dedicated customers seeing >10% errors at peak; support tickets created, status page updated.
- Actions outstanding: monitor infra reboot, validate node rejoin or proceed with reprovision, monitor error rate and throttles, follow up with account owners after stabilization.

alex: jin — I'm leaving detailed logs and the commands run in the incident doc. Take over and ping here if anything regresses.

jin: taking over. Thanks alex. I'll keep the thread updated. Current plan: wait for infra reboot result, if node rejoins run kubelet/system logs collection, otherwise proceed with reprovision. I'll also verify ingress routing and TTLs for cached entries.

maria: thanks all. I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and escalate to sales for affected accounts if needed.

samir: adding note: postmortem candidate if hardware root-cause confirmed. We should capture how many pods used local cache and consider shard replication changes.

ops-bot: Handoff recorded — oncall transferred to jin at 02:40 UTC.

jin: quick check-in: infra reports node reboot completed, but node not yet registered with k8s. Running remote diagnostics now. Will update within 10m.

alex: thanks everyone. leaving the channel for next steps.

-- end of thread --
